Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

Most of San Francisco city workers are set to get 12% raises over the next four years, plus a guarantee of no layoffs — despite a projected $450 million deficit for the 2029 fiscal year.

Mayor Daniel Lurie and ten unions representing about 25,000 city workers reached a surprise labor deal Tuesday with those terms ahead of the June 30 expiration of the unions’ current contract, three months after he handed out similar raises to cops and firefighters as part of a record $17 billion budget.

“We put forward a contract extension that honors their work, provides stability and recognizes the cost-of-living increases affecting so many San Franciscans,” Lurie said in a statement.
